linkedin.name: Sophia Amoruso
linkedin.headline: Founder & Managing Partner at Trust Fund. Investor in Lovable, Wispr Flow, Superhuman, Eight Sleep, Nectar Social, Liquid Death, Public.com, and 45+ startups. Built Nasty Gal to $100M+. Wrote NYT Bestseller #GIRLBOSS.
linkedin.about:
I'm the Founder & Managing Partner at Trust Fund, an early-stage venture fund backing software companies that help people and teams start, manage, and scale businesses. Our founders are killers building painkillers. 

Our LPs include Marc Andreessen, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks, Jeremy Liew, Andrew Chen, Chris Dixon, Jeff Jordan, Ev Williams, Paris Hilton, and Phil Hellmuth. 

Previously wrote an 18-week New York Times Bestseller, #GIRLBOSS, which was adapted into a scripted Netflix series that premiered on Netﬂix, produced by Charlize Theron. 

Started fashion e-tailer Nasty Gal at 22 years old and bootstrapped it to $30 million profitably, raised $60 million from Index Ventures and Thrive Capital, then scaled it to over $100 million in revenue. 

Went on the victory lap and was featured on the cover of Forbes magazine's 2016 America's Richest Self-Made Women issue (returned the dress I wore in the photo) and featured in the Fortune 40 under 40, Forbes 30 under 30, Inc. 30 under 30, and Fast Company’s Most Creative People in Business lists. 

My interests include drinking coffee on an empty stomach, choosing the best seats on commercial aircraft, and harvesting my hard-won experience for the next generation of founders.

In 2013, I wrote my first angel check. It was for $99,994.45, and into a vintage and antiques marketplace called 1stDibs. A year prior, that was by far the most amount of money I'd ever seen in my personal bank account.

To say my financial trajectory was whiplash is an understatement — it was whiplash of biblical proportions. I was shot from the bowels of San Francisco's Taqueria Cancun onto the cover of Forbes Magazine, invited to tables I never knew existed, and seated next to Silicon Valley's finest.

I snuck in the back door to this endlessly fascinating world of ideas and innovation. As a founder, it's given me the ability to fundraise, recruit, and tap domain experts of all kinds. As an angel investor, it's given me a network of deal flow to invest in some pretty amazing early-stage companies.

However, it's a network that rarely opens for people like me. For whom it does, there's a type.

You know the pedigree: they studied at Harvard, went to work at Goldman Sachs, and partied in Montauk before signing up as a venture associate to invest in alongside their b-school cronies, lobbing opportunities back and forth. They set themselves up to get rich together. So fucking smart.

I hate to admit it, but over the years I've envied those guys. If I'd been one, perhaps my companies would have been more successful. If I'd been cronies with them, maybe I'd have avoided a few missteps.

This is all to say that I'm not a trust fund baby. And you likely aren't either. That's where Trust Fund comes in. Today marks the debut of Trust Fund, a venture fund focused on early-stage technology-enabled consumer businesses that make people's work and personal lives better. Think cheaper, faster, richer, healthier, more connected, more productive, longer, more sustainable.

And in non-traditional fashion, I’m inviting founders, operators, creators, creatives, marketers, and other strategic folks to invest alongside me.

I’ve reserved $1 million for accredited investors join me and existing investors like @parishilton @evhead @jason @thesamparr and Marc Andreessen as limited partners, with a minimum check size of $2,000.

Learn and and apply at my link in bio.
